sources.citation: Soucy, Gil & Erin Soucy (comps.). 2017. Diccionario del zapoteco de Quiavicuzas / Quiavicuzas Zapotec - Spanish - English dictionary, print edition (PDF '', 43 pp., c. 1,108 entries, created 2017-09-01). SIL International, Webonary.org. Language expert: Arturo Martinez (Santiago Quiavicuzas).
sources.note: No prose at all (the PDF is the bare A-Z dictionary body, no introduction or notes). Every headword carries an IPA transcription in which each syllable bears a Chao tone letter: census over the text = mid [˧] 1497, high [˥] 626, low [˩] 108, falling [˥˩] 92, rising [˩˥] 31 (plus a handful of ˧˥/˥˧/˥˨), e.g. 'beal [bæl˩] pescado', 'baat [baːtʰ˥] pato', 'si [si˥˩] silla', 'yoʼ2 [jɔːʔ˩˥] casa', 'yuu [juː˥˩] tierra'; tonal minimal pairs are numbered (pkeatsil1 [pkæ˥tsɪl˧] 'escondido (futuro)' vs pkeatsil2 [pkæ˧tsɪl˧] 'escondido (pasado)'). Glottalized/laryngealized vowels and fortis sonorants are…

sources.citation: INALI. 2008. Catálogo de las lenguas indígenas nacionales: variantes lingüísticas de México con sus autodenominaciones y referencias geoestadísticas. Diario Oficial de la Federación, 14 January 2008 (segunda sección), Zapotec section.
sources.note: Nothing. Lists the variant <zapoteco de Quiavicuzas> with autonyms ditsere' [dit͡seɾeʔ] and dixhtiò [diʃtio˨], spoken only in Santiago Quiavicuzas (San Carlos Yautepec); San Juan Lachixila and other Nejapa de Madero localities are assigned to <zapoteco de Sierra sur, del noreste alto> (dichsà/didzá/ditsáh), and Guadalupe Guevea to <zapoteco de la montaña del Istmo, alto>. The tone letters in the phonetic autonyms are the only prosodic information.

sources.note: Related variety only (Guevea de Humboldt, zpg/guev1238, a sister Transyautepecan language): a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned confirms stem-final stress in compounds ('the first element loses its stress'; nucleus/tone neutralization in 'prestressed syllables'; syllabic enclitics 'secondarily stressed'). Does not mention Quiavicuzas.
